$description: Ergo Light — tool-agnostic design tokens. Layer 1 (primitive ramps) + Layer 2 (semantic roles). Adapters in theme/generate.py translate semantic tokens into per-tool files; no tool reads this file directly. Ramps rebuilt in OKLCH: an eased perceptual L* ladder (steps compress toward the light end so background tints get more resolution), a single locked hue per ramp, and one shared chroma ceiling (~0.061 across the ink steps 300-700) so every accent carries equal weight. Light-end steps 100/200 sit on a three-tier tint scale — whisper ~1.13:1, standard ~1.30:1, strong ~1.55:1 vs paper — so state washes read across displays, not just calibrated ones; those wash steps are additionally desaturated (C≈0.026) so they read as quiet tinted paper rather than colour blocks (see primitive.$description for the two-regime chroma model and the amber exception). Direction: calm neutral paper (one shared bg), soft ink ~10:1, muted 'dusty' accents (uniform low chroma, ~4.9:1 at the .600 step), very soft near-neutral background tints.

primitive.$description: Layer 1 — raw color ramps, hue + lightness (50 lightest, 900 darkest). Eased in perceptual L* (steps compress toward the light end) with a single locked hue. TWO CHROMA REGIMES by design: light steps (50-200) are near-neutral background tints (C≈0.008-0.026 — softened so state washes read as quiet tinted paper, not colour blocks), then chroma steps up to a normal 'ink' plateau (C≈0.06) across 300-700 for AA-readable foregrounds and the diff word-emph / active-search 'pop' tier. The 200→300 chroma jump (~+0.034) is intentional, not a break — backgrounds stay quiet, foregrounds carry hue; the seam lands exactly on the wash→pop boundary. Amber's light end is the deliberate exception (~2x the other tints' chroma) because a desaturated ~90° yellow greys to dirty olive. Meaningless on their own; semantic tokens give them roles.

gray.$description: Neutral grey (hue stripped, C*≈0) — every surface, border, and ink tone. Was 'barely-warm' but the warm hue put a yellow film over the whole editor; neutralised at identical lightness so all contrasts hold. base (50) is the single shared environment background for nvim, terminal and zellij; a soft off-white (not stark) so it reads calm, not glary.

red.$description: Errors, deletions, and the warm mode-accent.

amber.$description: Warm gold ramp — comment/search/diff-change washes (light) and warnings (dark). Light steps are pinned to ~78° (warm gold), NOT pure yellow ~90°: a desaturated 90° yellow greys toward dirty olive/khaki, so the softened light-end tints are rotated warmer to read as clean wheat/cream. Light-end also carries ~2x the chroma of the other ramps' tints — yellow needs more chroma than green/blue/red to read as a clean hue rather than muddy grey at the same lightness. Dark steps ease to ~72° gold.

semantic.$description: Layer 2 — roles in the Ergo Light language. Tool-agnostic: these describe meaning (a surface, an error, a string), never a tool. Every value is an alias into a primitive ramp so the whole system re-tunes from Layer 1.

base.$description: shared background for editor, terminal and zellij — soft neutral paper

cursorline.$description: current-line highlight — stepped to gray.200 so it is actually visible on paper

popup.$description: popup / telescope bg — one step off base so it reads as a layer, not just a border

primary.$description: body text / default fg — soft neutral dark (~10:1), calm not harsh

muted.$description: hints, line numbers, muted UI (comments use comment.fg)

constant.$description: constants, numbers, booleans — dropped one step from violet.600 so a lightness cue survives the blue↔violet hue collapse under deuteranopia/protanopia (function stays at blue.600; without the offset the two are indistinguishable for red-green CVD)

link.$description: links / urls — dropped to blue.800 so constant can stay vivid at violet.700 without the two colliding under CVD (link and constant share a hue axis but never the same buffer)

error.$description: errors — darkest red, 2 steps below the warm mode-accent so the two never read alike

primary.$description: active selection — stepped to blue.300 (strong tier, ~1.56:1) so it separates from the neutral current-line highlight (cursorline = gray.200 sits at the same lightness; at blue.200 the two collided at ΔE 0.026). A selection is a transient interactive state meant to be seen, so it carries ink-tier chroma, not the quiet wash chroma.

soft.$description: search match bg — stepped up so matches read on paper

fg.$description: comment foreground — aliased to text.secondary (same weight); comments are signal, meant to be read

bg.$description: normal comment band — soft light yellow

high.$description: high-priority comment markers (TODO/FIXME/WARNING/NOTE) — the deeper 'attention' amber, shared with diff-changed lines, so must-see notes out-shout ordinary comments

add.$description: added lines — standard-tier tint (~1.30:1 on paper) so the wash reads across displays, not just calibrated ones

addText.$description: word-level emphasis inside an added line (delta plus-emph / nvim DiffText) — one step above the line tint (strong tier) so the changed word out-reads the line

change.$description: changed/modified lines (nvim DiffChange) — the 'attention' amber (deeper than the normal comment band). Add/delete stay rose/mint (git-standard red/green); changed is amber. The comment band is suppressed inside diffs so this never nests with comment yellow.

changeText.$description: uniform with the changed line — no darker word-patch.

delete.$description: deleted lines — standard-tier tint (~1.30:1), mirrors diff.add

deleteText.$description: word-level emphasis inside a deleted line (delta minus-emph) — strong tier, mirrors diff.addText

primary.$description: primary cursor block — kept near-black so the caret stays easy to spot

terminal.$description: The ANSI palette is a role a terminal plays, not a tool. Muted on purpose vs the editor accents. On a light theme the 'white' channels are the awkward ones — a light 'white' can't also be legible as text on light paper, so both are pulled dark enough to survive as text: white=gray.600 (5.1:1, AA) and bright.white=gray.500 (3.4:1, AA-large, still one step lighter than white to keep 15-brighter-than-7 ordering).
